column1: # MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS references for each kind of finding the fleet result names, shown by
# gird-intune.ps1 -Report. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
# The mapping is Blindspot's own, not MITRE's. Blindspot reads files: it never detects a technique in use.
#   word       a finding word of the fleet inventory value, as gird-intune.ps1's $ItemOrder lists it. Every
#              word has at least one attack line and one atlas line, mapped or none (gen.sh refuses a word
#              without one, and a word gird-intune.ps1 does not know)
#   os         all, mac or win: the line applies only to results from that system (a Windows result
#   scope      all, or the incident ids (data/incidents.tsv) the line applies to, comma separated: only
#              for a word whose value lists incident ids (incidents, lockfile, update, remove). The report
#              shows such a line only for PCs whose result names one of them
#   id         the technique id, or - on a none line
#   name       the technique's name as MITRE's page gives it (a sub-technique as parent: name), or -
#   tactics    the tactics MITRE lists for the technique, comma separated, or -
#   relation   exposure: Blindspot found something the technique could exploit
#              indicator: a trace that a published incident links to the technique
#              armed: installed, and carries the technique out when triggered
#              none: no technique fits; the note says why
#   note       on a none line, why no technique fits, as the report shows it; - otherwise
# Read on 18 November 2026: ATT&CK Enterprise v20.1 (https://attack.mitre.org/resources/versions/, current
# since 13 October 2026), each technique's page; ATLAS release 2026.10 of 28 October 2026, from the data the
#   wiper: T1543.002 Systemd Service (Linux only, and the fleet result comes from macOS and Windows) and
#   T1053.005 Scheduled Task (what Blindspot finds on Windows is a folder, not a scheduled task).
#   incidents: T1543.001 and T1543.002 for an incident's startup file (the result does not say which file
#   planted: AML.T0010.001, which fits only lightning's payload; the result gives a count, not the incident.
# T1698 Indirect Prompt Injection lists SaaS and Windows as its platforms, so it is for Windows results only.
# AML.T0010.001 names T1195.002 as its ATT&CK counterpart; ATT&CK itself places npm and Python packages
# under T1195.001, which these lines follow.
